questions.question: On which date is National Sports Day observed in India?
questions.solution:
**The Correct Answer is __Option 1__ i.e __29th August__.**

 
• **National Sports Day is celebrated every year on 29th August.**
 
• It is celebrated to commemorate the birth anniversary of hockey legend **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• On this day, President of India honors eminent sports personalities with major awards including Khel Ratna, Arjuna Awards, Dronacharya Awards, and Dhyan Chand Award.
 
• **Dhyan Chand**: Born on August 29, 1905, Dhyan Chand is considered the greatest hockey player of all time.
 
 
• Born in Uttar Pradesh, Chand earned three Olympic gold medals in 1928, 1932 and 1936 in field hockey.
 
• He was conferred the Padma Bhushan award.

questions.question: 'Torr' is a unit of _______.
questions.solution:
**The Correct Answer is __Option 2__ i.e __pressure__.**

 
• **Pressure**: The **pressure **is defined as force per unit area. 

 
 
• A **torr **is a **non-SI unit** of **pressure** defined as 1/760 of an atmosphere.
 
• **pascal (Pa), is the SI unit of pressure.**
 
 
 
• **Power**: The rate of doing work is called power.
 
 
• The SI unit of power is the Watt. 
 
 
 
• **Energy**: Capacity of doing work by a body is called its energy.
 
 
• SI unit of energy is Joule.
 
 
 
• **Force**: Any action which causes push or pull on a body is called force.
 
 
• The Newton is the SI unit of force.
 
• There are four basic forces in nature. They are:
 
 
• Gravitational Forces
 
• Weak Nuclear Forces
 
• Electromagnetic Forces
 
• Strong Nuclear Forces

questions.question: Who appoints the Advocate General of states?

options.text: Chief Justice of the high court

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __Option 3__ i.e __Governor of the state__.

 
• Advocate General of states:

 
 
• Article 165 of the constitution talks about the Advocate General of states.
 
• He is the highest law officer in the state. 
 
• He assists the state government in all its legal matters.
 
• The Governor of each State shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court to be an Advocate-General for the State.
 
• The Advocate-General shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor. 
 
• He shall receive such remuneration as the Governor may determine.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister of the state:** Chief Minister of a state of India is the 'elected' head of the government and the executive authority lies with the Chief Minister. 
 
 
• He is appointed by the respective State Governor.
 
 
 
• **President of India:** He is the supreme commander of the Indian armed forces.
 
 
• The qualifications to become a president are: 
 
 
• He should be a citizen of India,
 
• He must have completed 35 years of age.
 
• He must be qualified to become a member of Lok Sabha.
 
• He should not hold any office of profit under the Union or state government.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Governor of the state: **
 
 
• He is the constitutional head of the state.
 
• He is appointed by the president.
 
• He must have at least 35 years of age to become a governor.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of the high court:**
 
 
• He is appointed by the President in consultation with the Chief justice of India as well as the Governor of the state concerned.

__
 
• **Osmium (Atomic Number: 76)**:

 
 
• At the modest temperatures and pressures of Earth’s surface, the **densest** known material is the metallic element **osmium**

questions.question: What is the velocity of sound in air?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

Sound: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a3d091101a3e017a03bdeafac0606d42d4d8f7c65fa313187b24b1c9105761d.png] 

__
 
• A local disturbance whose propagation is facilitated by the **collisions between particles**, this disturbance propagates in a **longitudinal wave**, imagine one molecule hitting the next molecule, and then that molecule hitting the next, and so forth.

 
 
• It is a mechanical wave that needs a medium to travel.
 
• The speed of sound is maximum in solid then it is in liquid and slowest in gases.
 
 

**EXPLANATION__:**

 
• The **speed of sound **is actually the **speed of transmission of a small disturbance through a medium** i.e the rate at which sound travels through a medium.
 
• Sound **cannot travel in a vacuum** as there is **no medium for the sound to travel through**.
 
• The **speed of sound in air **is about** 332 meters per second**.
 
• Sound travels **fastest** in **solids (such as steel)**, then **liquid**, and then **least in gases**.

questions.question: Who among the following scholars is associated with the Tibet-home theory of the Aryans?
questions.solution:
**The Correct Answer is __Option 4__ i.e __​Dayanand Saraswati__.**

 
• **Swami Dayanand** **Saraswati** in Satyarth Prakash gave the** Tibet home theory** that **Tibet **was the original home of the Aryans.
 
• **Max** **Muller** in central Asian theory propounded that **central Asia **was the original home of the Aryans.
 
 
• His opinion was that the information, regarding the early Aryans, could be gathered from two main sources. They are Vedic literature and the Iranian book Zend-Avesta. 
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar** **Tilak** put forward the Arctic region theory in which he propounded that the **Arctic** **region** was the original home of Aryans.
 
 
• His view is that the description of the natural phenomenon in Rigveda tallies with that of the region of North-Pole.

questions.question: The Mission of the Ramsar Convention is to conserve __________.
questions.solution:
**The Co
rrect Answer is __Option 2__ i.e __wetlands__.**

 
• **Ramsar Convention:**

 
 
• The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty for the conservation and wise use of **wetlands**.
 
• It is named after the **Iranian city of Ramsar**, on the Caspian Sea, where the treaty was signed on 2 February 1971.
 
• it is also known as the wetlands convention.
 
• As of July 2021, there are 42 wetlands in India that have international importance and are hence recognized as the Ramsar Sites in India.
 
• The newly added 10 new Ramsar sites in India are:
 
 
• Maharashtra gets its first Ramsar site (Nandur Madhameshwar), Punjab which already had 3 Ramsar sites adds 3 more (Keshopur-Miani, Beas Conservation Reserve, Nangal) and UP with 1 Ramsar site has added 6 more (Nawabganj, Parvati Agra, Saman, Samaspur, Sandi and SarsaiNawar).
 
 
 
 
 
• United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) provides the overarching framework for the governance of the oceans.
